Application Materials.content:
Make sure that you upload clear scanned copies of your degree certificate (if completed) and final or current transcript, as well as any other supporting documents. We will not be able to assess your application without them. Please do not send us the original copies in the post, as we will be unable to return these.
Depending on the course you are applying for, you may also need to provide two references, including at least one who can comment on your academic ability. These must be dated within two years of the date of your application and, if not submitted directly by your referee, signed and on letter-headed paper.
We may also require a personal statement. If you aren't sure what to include or need more help, please refer to our [guidance](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/careers/students/furtherstudy/applying.aspx "Writing a personal statement for further study") or [contact us](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/help-and-support/home/contact-us.html).
Your application provides an opportunity for you to articulate the skills and experiences you have that make you suitable for a place on our courses. AI tools may help structure things such as personal statements, or check for readability, but generating all, or a large part of your application submissions and communications regarding your application, using an AI tool and presenting this as your own work or words could affect the outcome of your application.
Admissions may, at their discretion, ask applicants to provide further information in order to assess their application fairly and accurately. This can include CVs, references (academic and professional) and clarifications regarding their previous and current education.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Entry requirement: **2:1 (or international equivalent) in any discipline**; applicants should not have previously studied a significant amount of business analytics, but must have a **strong 2:1 (65%) in quantitative modules at degree level with a significant amount of mathematical/statistical content**.
- Alternative qualifications: applicants are treated on an individual basis, and relevant work experience may also be considered.
- China applicants: applicants should hold a bachelors degree of a good standard from a recognised university, usually in a relevant subject area. Entry requirements for degrees from Chinese universities vary depending on the university studied at and the course applied for.
- China applicants: depending on the tiers of institutions applicants graduated from, Chinese grade equivalence varies. For a **2:1**, the stated range is **72% - 80%**.
- China applicants: HND/SQA AD (**BB/BBB/60%/Merit**) + final year/top-ups to a UK Bachelor degree studied in the UK only, and 3 years Chinese Junior Diploma (Dazhuan) + 1/2 years final years/top-ups to a Bachelor degree may be accepted as long as applicants meet the grade requirement, e.g. **2.1**, in both parts of the programme.
- China applicants: Bachelor degrees obtained via **2-year China Diploma plus 1-year top-up in the UK cannot be accepted** by any Departments/Schools at UoN.
- China applicants: for a **3+1 joint programme**, the university would expect an offer to be made on the second part, but applicants must also have achieved the requirement, e.g. **2:1**, in part 1 of the programme. For a **2+2 joint programme**, the decision will be made only based on overseas transcripts.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
- IELTS: **6.5 (no less than 6.0 in each element)**.
- As well as IELTS, the University also accepts other [English language qualifications](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/international-applicants/english-language.aspx), including **TOEFL iBT, Pearson PTE, GCSE, IB and O level English**.
- If you need support to meet the required level, you may be able to attend a presessional English course. If you successfully complete your presessional course to the required level, you can then progress to your degree course and **won't need to retake IELTS or equivalent**.
- For on-campus presessional English courses, you must take **IELTS for UKVI** to meet visa regulations. For online presessional courses, see the CELE [webpages](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/cele/presessional/index.aspx) for guidance.
- For China (mainland) applicants: if you successfully completed a UK Degree **within two years of the University of Nottingham course start date**, where at least one full academic year was physically taught in the UK, this would usually satisfy the English language requirements of your course.

Program Overview.content:
Business Analytics MSc is a **full-time, 12-month** programme starting in **September 2027**; part-time study is not available.
The MSc in Business Analytics is designed with input from top multinational companies to build technical and business skills for data-driven decision-making. The programme is delivered by the [Neo-demographic Laboratory for Analytics in Business (N/LAB)](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/businesscentres/n-lab/index.aspx), an advanced research and teaching facility within the Business School. Students benefit from N/LAB’s strong industry ties, accessing real-world datasets and insights from global partners.
The course develops specialist technical skills and strategic thinking, preparing students as data scientists equipped with:
- skills to implement advanced data science methods using big data tools
- practical experience of delivering business analytics projects using real-world case studies
- managerial and communication skills to lead data-driven decision-making
Students get access to advanced facilities including secure computer environments, 3D visualisation technology and an immersive video wall for advanced research and analytics projects.
The Business School is triple accredited, part of an elite group of business schools worldwide with ‘triple crown’ accreditation: [EQUIS](https://www.efmdglobal.org/accreditations/business-schools/equis/), [AMBA](https://www.associationofmbas.com/) and [AACSB](https://www.aacsb.edu/). The course is delivered by N/LAB, which provides state-of-the-art research, data visualisation and teaching facilities. Business School students also have the opportunity to gain digital skills with industry-recognised [Microsoft and SAP certifications](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/study-with-us/digital-professional-skills/index.aspx).
Across the autumn and spring semesters, students take **120 credits** of taught modules. They complete a **60-credit dissertation** over the summer and are allocated an appropriate dissertation supervisor. The summer project represents the culmination of the programme, requiring students to design, execute and report a research project based on the analysis of real-world or simulated data. There is also an option of a Business Project, subject to availability and a student selection process.
Teaching takes place through lectures, seminars, tutorials and workshops. Assessment is by dissertation, examinations and coursework. Students have at least a weekly average of **8 timetabled hours** through lectures, seminars and workshops, tutorials or supervision.
The programme is based at [Jubilee Campus](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/about/campuses/jubileecampus.aspx), home to the university’s business, education and computer science schools.
With tailored [careers support](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/business/careers-and-employability/careers-support-for-masters-students.aspx), many master’s students go on to secure roles with world-leading employers. Recent graduates have been hired by companies such as Allianz, Amazon, Boots, KPMG and Unilever. The Business School Postgraduate Careers team provides advice, guidance and coaching, and the Accelerated Career Leader Programme is integrated within the MSc. Graduate destinations for postgraduates include business analysts, data analysts, management consultants, finance and investment analysts and advisers, business development managers, financial managers, marketing associate professionals, human resources managers and accountants. Some MSc graduates have gone on to doctoral studies, while others have become entrepreneurs. The average starting salary for postgraduates in Nottingham University Business School was **£38,931**.

Curriculum.content:
Business Analytics MSc is offered **full-time: 12 months**; **part-time: Not available**.
Across the autumn and spring semesters, students take **120 credits of taught modules**. Students complete a **60-credit dissertation** over the summer and are allocated an appropriate dissertation supervisor.
Semester one core modules:
- Foundational Business Analytics
- Data at Scale: Management, Processing and Visualisation
Semester one optional modules: one from:
- Entrepreneurship in Context
- Management Science for Decision Support
- Supply Chain Planning and Management
Semester two core modules:
- Analytics Specialisations and Applications
- Leading Big Data Business Projects
- Machine Learning and Predictive Analytics
Semester two optional modules: one from:
- Advanced Operations Analysis
- Digital Marketing
Summer:
- Data Driven Dissertation Project in Business Analytics: students design, execute and report a research project based on the analysis of real-world or simulated data, including an **8,000-word dissertation**, exhibits and data visualisations.
- Business Project: requires students, working as groups, to undertake research in a topic relevant to business, management, marketing, finance, accounting, or information system; the topic must be relevant to the named degree programme and is subject to formal approval. Option of a Business Project is subject to availability and a student selection process.
Modules are assessed by a combination of exams and coursework at the end of the relevant semester. Students have at least a weekly average of **8 timetabled hours** through lectures, seminars and workshops, tutorials or supervision. As a guide, a **20 credit module is approximately 200 hours of work** combined teaching and self-study.
Learning methods include lectures, seminars, tutorials and workshops. Assessment methods include dissertation, examinations and coursework.
The course is taught at **Jubilee Campus**.

Financial Aid.content:
Automatic scholarships for international master's students. At the University of Nottingham, scholarships worth **£3,000** are offered to students starting their studies in **2026**. **This will be automatically awarded and will be deducted from your master's tuition fee.** Enrol. Automatically receive £3,000 scholarship. No scholarship application needed.
Eligibility: You must:
- be an international fee-paying student
- be starting year one of a full-time postgraduate taught master's degree programme (UK campus-based)
- be studying towards one of the following awards: MA, **MSc**, MArch, MBA, LLM, MPA, MPH or MMedSci
- be self-funded, and not in receipt of any other University award or sponsorship by an external organisation
Note: for a two year master's degree the scholarship only applies to the first year's fees. The university reserves the right of awarding scholarships and some exceptions may apply. [See full terms and conditions](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/international-applicants/scholarships-funding-finance/termsconditions.aspx "International scholarship terms and conditions"). Students progressing to the University from Kaplan (University of Nottingham International College or Digital Pathways) are not eligible for this scholarship scheme. However, students may be eligible for Kaplan - University of Nottingham specific scholarships.

Deferral Admission Policy.content:
You can request a deferral of your postgraduate offer to the next academic year, providing that:
- the course accepts deferred entry
- you have accepted your offer
- you have met any academic and reference conditions on the offer within the [deadline](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/pgstudy/already-applied/offer.aspx#deadlines "I have an offer") to do so
- you have paid any [tuition fee deposits](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/fabs/finance/frequentlyaskedquestions/casfaq.aspx "Tuition fee deposits - Frequently Asked Questions") if it's required - most postgraduate taught courses require international students to pay a deposit for visa purposes
Postgraduate Taught (PGT) and Postgraduate Research (PGR) change of start dates can be requested through [our enquiry form](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/studywithus/enquiry.aspx "Make an enquiry"). Please include your full name and University of Nottingham ID number. The deadline to request this is **one day after the latest date to register**.
Deferral requests will be considered by the university and are not guaranteed. We may need to refer to the individual school or the academic supervisor (for postgraduate research courses) before confirming. Offers are usually confirmed once all necessary deposits have been paid and offer details for the following year are available.
Ordinarily, you can only defer the same offer **once**. If you still cannot attend in the following year and want to study the course another year later, you would need to make a new application.
If you are considering or have requested a deferral, you should not complete registration processes for your course in the current year as deferrals cannot be processed once you have registered as a student.
[Complete the Deferral Request Form](https://app.geckoform.com/public/#/modern/21FO00hzsr9ok800es8ni3yxsc)
The university does not usually defer scholarship offers to the following year. If we've offered you a scholarship, this will be withdrawn and you would need to reapply for scholarships in the following year.
International students who will be sponsored by an external organisation will usually have their [student visa CAS deposit](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/fabs/finance/frequentlyaskedquestions/cas-deposits.aspx#sponsor "Student visa CAS deposits - Frequently Asked Questions") waived after providing evidence of sponsorship for the relevant course and academic year. If you need to defer your studies, you must provide a new letter or written confirmation from your sponsor, confirming that your sponsorship will be still be valid in the next academic year. If you cannot provide this confirmation, you must pay the deposit to defer your offer.
We are unable to support deposit waivers for Chevening or Commonwealth Scholarship applicants deferring an offer. If you intend to fund your deferred study via an application to one of these bodies and have not had confirmation of an award, you must pay the appropriate deposit in order to defer your offer.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
If you need support to meet the required English level, you may be able to attend a [presessional English course](https://www.nottingham.ac.uk/cele/presessional/index.aspx). If you successfully complete your presessional course to the required level, you can then progress to your degree course; this means that you won't need to retake IELTS or equivalent.
For students studying a 3+1 joint programme, Nottingham would expect an offer to be made on their second part, but students must also have achieved the requirement, for example **2:1**, in part 1 of their programme. If students are studying a 2+2 joint programme, the decision will be made only based on their overseas transcripts.
